purpose: Authoritative-vendor evidence delta adding three process-control/DCS integration targets: Emerson DeltaV Edge Environment, Yokogawa CENTUM VP/Exaopc, and Honeywell Experion PKS/Hybrid SCADA. Reuses existing REST and OPC UA profiles, keeps all routes read-only and customer-edge constrained, and does not claim authenticated tenant or round-trip evidence. No credentials, customer data, writes, control actions or plant-network probes were used.

systems.name: Emerson DeltaV / DeltaV Edge Environment
systems.evidenceNote: Emerson documents DeltaV Edge Environment as a secure, one-way/outbound, read-only replica of DeltaV data that preserves configuration hierarchy/context and exposes enterprise access through REST API and OPC UA. The same environment can host applications/scripts, but WFM reuses only the existing REST and OPC UA read profiles. Direct DCS access, script/application execution, configuration and process-control authority remain outside the connector boundary.

requiredPermissions: customer-approved read-only DeltaV Edge identity or OPC UA certificate scoped to the approved site/data set
read access only to contextualized process values, equipment hierarchy, alarms/events and recent runtime data required for workforce decisions
customer/site edge routing for protected OT deployments; prefer the DeltaV Edge replicated enterprise-side copy rather than direct DCS connectivity
no application/script execution, DCS configuration, control command, write, engineering or management-plane authority
dataAvailableOrExpected: contextualized DeltaV runtime/process values exposed through the Edge replica
DeltaV configuration hierarchy and metadata that preserve plant/unit/equipment relationships
near-real-time operational state and recent runtime data
alarm/operational context where exposed to the approved Edge data set
enterprise-side REST/OPC UA data suitable for correlation with WFM shifts, production and maintenance records
automationOpportunities: refresh labour recovery/redeployment recommendations when process or equipment state shows a stoppage, constraint or recovery
correlate staffed hours, overtime and skills mix with process throughput and downtime without giving WFM control-system authority
trigger qualified maintenance coverage from approved alarm/condition signals while leaving work execution and DCS actions in their source systems
reuse DeltaV hierarchy/context during implementation to map plant, unit and work-centre structure more quickly
combine process state with production schedules to improve short-horizon staffing forecasts and paid-idle detection
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle time and avoidable overtime by reacting to actual process state instead of static schedules
reduce downtime duration by surfacing workforce/skills coverage needs from operational context sooner
reduce integration engineering by consuming the contextualized Edge hierarchy rather than rebuilding flat-tag relationships manually
improve labour-to-output and labour-to-downtime attribution for operations and finance
dataGaps: DeltaV is not normally authoritative for worker identity, payroll, contractual hours, absence, agency commercials or formal qualifications
the exact REST resource model, authentication mechanism, pagination/rate limits and OPC UA namespace available to a customer depend on deployed DeltaV/Edge versions and configuration
process tags do not inherently identify which worker caused or resolved a condition and must not be used as sole worker-performance evidence
long-term history may live in a separate historian and may require a different approved integration path
constraintsRisks: DeltaV is a safety/production-critical control environment; WFM must never scan or connect directly to the control network when a customer-approved Edge/DMZ projection is available
OPC UA can support write-capable methods in some deployments; WFM must restrict itself to Browse/Read/Subscribe and validate certificate trust, endpoint identity and security policy
DeltaV Edge includes an execution sandbox and scripting capability; data access must not inherit script, application-deployment or management authority
schema/tag/hierarchy changes and site-specific naming require fingerprints, versioned mappings, quality/status preservation and stale-data detection
near-real-time replicated data can be delayed during connectivity faults; source/event time, ingestion time and freshness must remain explicit
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Keep DeltaV at spec verification. In an authorised customer environment, prove the DeltaV Edge topology and version, establish a least-privilege read identity/certificate, enumerate REST/OPC UA metadata without direct DCS scanning, validate pagination/rate limits or subscription behaviour, fingerprint hierarchy/tag mappings, test stale/replay handling, and normalise only approved process/alarm/state context before promoting evidence.

systems.name: Yokogawa CENTUM VP / Exaopc
systems.evidenceNote: Yokogawa documents Exaopc R3.82 (November 2025) with OPC UA server functions for Data Access and Alarms & Conditions, secure communications and support for CENTUM VP R6.12 and R7.01. WFM therefore reuses the existing OPC UA edge profile for read/subscription only. No CENTUM control, engineering or write operations are inferred or enabled.

requiredPermissions: customer-approved Exaopc OPC UA endpoint and certificate/trust configuration scoped to the approved plant/site
Browse/Read/Subscribe access only to approved data values, alarms/conditions and equipment context
customer/site edge termination; no cloud-side scan of Vnet/IP or the process-control network
no OPC UA write/method execution, CENTUM engineering, alarm acknowledgement, control or configuration authority
dataAvailableOrExpected: CENTUM process values exposed through Exaopc OPC UA Data Access
alarms and conditions exposed through the Exaopc OPC UA A&C server where configured
plant/unit/equipment tags and operational state represented in the customer OPC namespace
timestamps/status/quality information available through the OPC UA data model
automationOpportunities: use approved process/alarm state to recommend redeployment when a unit is constrained or unavailable
surface qualified maintenance or operations coverage needs from alarm/condition evidence
join shift labour with equipment/process availability to quantify paid idle time and labour-to-output performance
learn recurring staffing patterns around plant startups, shutdowns and operational disturbances without issuing control commands
reuse OPC namespace/site hierarchy mappings during implementation across CENTUM sites
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle time and overtime by aligning labour with actual plant availability
shorten downtime response by highlighting skill/coverage gaps as alarms and conditions emerge
reduce manual operational-to-WFM reconciliation through direct, read-only OPC UA context
improve cross-shift performance and finance attribution by relating labour conditions to process availability
dataGaps: CENTUM/Exaopc is not an authoritative source for payroll, absence, agency commercials, employment status or formal qualifications
customer OPC namespaces/tag naming and alarm configuration vary and require per-site discovery and mapping
public documentation does not establish the customer's exact certificate policy, endpoint URL, node permissions, sampling limits or subscription quotas
R6.12 and R7.01 support is documented for Exaopc R3.82, but older installed versions may expose different capabilities and must be detected rather than assumed
constraintsRisks: Exaopc bridges into a production DCS, so network segmentation and customer-edge termination are mandatory
OPC UA endpoints can expose write/method capabilities; WFM must permit only Browse/Read/Subscribe and fail closed on changed endpoint identity or certificates
alarm/event bursts require bounded subscriptions, deduplication, source timestamps and backpressure handling
intermittent edge connectivity can produce gaps or late data and must never masquerade as live state
schema/node drift across CENTUM/Exaopc upgrades requires namespace fingerprints and version-aware mapping
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Keep CENTUM VP/Exaopc at spec verification. In an authorised site or vendor sandbox, prove the Exaopc/CENTUM versions, endpoint identity and certificate trust, browse an allowlisted namespace, read/subscribe to a small representative set of DA and A&C nodes, validate quality/timestamp/reconnect/backpressure behaviour, fingerprint node mappings and keep all write/method/control operations denied before evidence promotion.

systems.name: Honeywell Experion PKS / Hybrid SCADA
systems.evidenceNote: Honeywell documents cloud-friendly OPC UA connectivity in Experion Hybrid SCADA together with native historian, real-time database, alarms/events and distributed-system data publication. Honeywell also documents OPC UA support on the Experion PKS server from R510 and HA support in R520, while current Experion releases continue the platform. WFM reuses only the OPC UA read/subscription edge profile and does not inherit controller, station, alarm-acknowledgement, engineering or control authority.

requiredPermissions: customer-approved OPC UA identity/certificate and endpoint limited to approved Experion sites/data
Browse/Read/Subscribe only for approved real-time points, alarms/events, history references and equipment/process context
customer/site edge or DMZ termination; prefer a read-only enterprise/remote gateway or approved OPC projection where available
no controller access, process writes, alarm acknowledgement, engineering, station operation, configuration or remote-control authority
dataAvailableOrExpected: real-time process/plant points and operational state exposed through approved OPC UA interfaces
alarm and event context available from Experion/Hybrid SCADA
historian/trending context and timestamps where exposed through the approved integration route
equipment/site relationships and Distributed System Architecture context across connected Experion systems
production-condition evidence that can be correlated with WFM shifts, staffing and maintenance data
automationOpportunities: recommend labour redeployment or recovery actions when equipment/process state shows downtime or constraint
surface maintenance/operations skills demand from approved alarms and condition evidence
correlate staffing, overtime and shift composition with plant uptime, output and alarm burden
use site/system hierarchy and DSA context to accelerate multi-site mapping without merging security domains
combine historical condition patterns with schedules to improve staffing forecasts for startups, shutdowns and recurrent disruptions
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle time and avoidable overtime by aligning labour decisions with real plant conditions
reduce downtime response time by connecting alarm/condition context to available skills and maintenance coverage
reduce manual SCADA-to-WFM reporting and improve labour-to-output/uptime attribution
improve multi-site implementation efficiency by reusing existing Experion hierarchy and DSA context where authorised
dataGaps: Experion is not normally authoritative for payroll, contractual hours, absence, agency commercials, employment status or formal qualifications
exact OPC UA objects, endpoint/security configuration, history exposure, node limits and subscription limits depend on Experion release and site configuration
R510/R511 are phased-out releases; installed-base version detection is required and older versions must not be assumed equivalent to current supported releases
operator/process events do not by themselves prove worker attendance, payable time or individual performance
constraintsRisks: Experion is a production-critical control platform and must remain behind customer-approved segmentation; no direct cloud scan or controller connection
OPC UA may coexist with control-capable interfaces and controllers; WFM must strictly allowlist read/subscription methods and validate endpoint identity/certificate/security mode
DSA can span multiple units/sites; WFM must preserve source-site/security-domain identity and must not use federation as permission to broaden reads
alarm/event bursts, historian backfill and reconnects require deduplication, backpressure, provenance and freshness controls
release differences such as R510/R520/R530 and customer-specific tag models require version-aware discovery and schema fingerprints
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Keep Experion at spec verification. In an authorised customer site or vendor environment, establish the deployed release/topology, use an approved read-only OPC UA/enterprise-side route, prove endpoint identity and least-privilege certificate permissions, browse/read/subscribe to a small allowlisted data set, validate alarm/event burst and reconnect behaviour, fingerprint site/tag mappings and keep all control/acknowledgement/engineering operations disabled before evidence promotion.
